items.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016
items.q: I had four musicians at the generation of McCoy. It was Herbie Hancock, it was McCoy Tyner, it was Chick Corea and it was Keith Jarrett. ... Those were my four most important.

ctx.x: Keith Jarrett is the principal. And many international — I mean they have a very special sound. I mean among the musicians you could talk about the ECM style, typically European. I wouldn’t say Keith Jarrett is too much into that but well he had a European group, as you know. But the ECM sound is typically Scandinavian and European.
Is it possible to put that into words? Is it less bluesy?
